current.text: The Warriors are reportedly treating this season as a gap year.
The team is worried about its lottery odds and may rest veterans, so this could be a throwaway season.
Experts see the roster as bad, especially early in the season. The roster is close to the same as last season.
Win projections range from about 43 wins down to a roughly .500 team with a bad downside. The betting win total of 40.5 sits in the middle of the league.
Warriors players are expected to fade as the season goes on.
Stephen Curry is the only player on the roster who gets real usage and creates his own shot. Santos may be a second, smaller shot creator.
Curry, Podziemski and Draymond Green are expected to start.
Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg is projected to start at forward.
The starting center is between Al Horford and Kristaps Porzingis. The newest projection starts Horford. Older notes start Porzingis when he is healthy.
The more Green plays center, the more minutes open up for Gui Santos and Lendeborg.
Santos and De'Anthony Melton are projected to come off the bench.
Depth is very poor. The team struggles to field a 10-man rotation, so minutes go up across the rotation.
The team has only 13 standard contracts and two two-way deals. It lost Quinten Post and Pat Spencer.
Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are out early in the season. Butler is out for at least half the season.
Butler's return will shake up the rotation again.
The team has 15 back-to-backs, more than most teams. That raises rest risk for Porzingis, Horford and Butler.
The fantasy playoff schedule is good: 11 games in weeks 19 to 21, with only one back-to-back in each week.

durable.text: Steve Kerr rarely starts rookies and has little patience for them.
Kerr runs unpredictable rotations. He often announces a set starting lineup and then changes it a few games later, with lots of mixing among the wings.

note: Curry carries all the shot creation, so his usage is safe. The risks are a possible gap year, 15 back-to-backs and veteran rest late in the season, even though the playoff schedule is good. Thin depth opens minutes for Podziemski, Lendeborg and Santos, and Butler is out for at least half the season. Early on, watch who starts at center (Horford or Porzingis), how often Green plays center, and whether Kerr keeps rookie Lendeborg in the starting five.
